# Escuminac, New Brunswick

Escuminac is a small fishing village located in northeastern New Brunswick, Canada, on the Miramichi Bay along the Northumberland Strait.

## Geography
- Situated on a peninsula extending into the Gulf of St. Lawrence
- Part of Hardwicke Parish in Northumberland County
- Located approximately 40 km east of Miramichi city

## Economy
- Historically dependent on the fishing industry, particularly lobster and crab
- Commercial fishing remains central to the local economy

## The Escuminac Disaster (1959)
The community is perhaps best known for the tragic **Escuminac Disaster of June 19-20, 1959**, when a sudden and violent storm struck the local fishing fleet:
- 35 fishermen from the area lost their lives
- 22 boats were destroyed
- It remains one of the worst fishing disasters in Canadian maritime history
- A memorial stands in the community to honor the victims
- The disaster led to improved weather forecasting and safety regulations for Maritime fishermen

## Demographics
- Small population, predominantly English-speaking
- Close-knit fishing community with deep generational ties to the area

## Notable Features
- Escuminac Wharf serves local fishermen
- The area has a lighthouse
- Known for its scenic coastal landscape
